$comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for anticipation-cache behavior, shared by the Python and JS/TS SDKs. Do not duplicate these values into either SDK's source. See ../README.md. Regexes are restricted to the intersection of Python 're' and ECMAScript; both SDKs have a parity test.

recall_bypass.note: WS4 of the playground query-hygiene plan. A recall-shaped question never serves from the anticipation cache. Asymmetric cost is why: a stale false-hit makes the agent answer 'I don't see that' while the store holds the fact (the BZQR6J cross-session failure), whereas bypassing costs only cold-fetch latency on a turn where the user already expects a lookup. Stem coverage cannot gate this — false hits were measured at coverage=1.00. Ties break toward INCLUDING a pattern.

patterns.note: Original set (WS4). 'again' alone is deliberately NOT a marker: 'book me a ride again' is a task query, not a recall query.
2026-07-16 eval register issue #11: 'can you confirm my email address?' served a stale bundle. Also catches 'confirm my booking' — an intentional over-match, costing one cloud fetch.
2026-07-16 eval register issue #11: 'what name is linked to my Uber account?' served a stale bundle.
2026-07-16 eval register issue #11: 'best way to contact me with updates' served a stale bundle.
2026-07-16 eval register issue #11, sibling phrasing of the above.
2026-07-16 eval register issue #11: 'which email are you going to use?' served a stale bundle.

bm25.note: Nominal threshold. The value actually applied is derived per query: max(effective_floor, min(bm25, query_token_scale * len(query_tokens))). Short queries cannot reach the nominal score, so holding them to it would miss every time.

novel_term.note: Fraction of query stems absent from the cached corpus that forces a miss.

min_corpus_for_novel_gate.note: The novel-term gate is meaningless on a small corpus, where the ratio is dominated by ordinary English word forms. Measured: a fresh playground conversation reaches ~60 stems after the first push and would trip the 0.45 gate on essentially every second-turn query. 200 means the gate engages once a customer has ~3-4 typical bundles cached.

effective_floor.note: Lower bound on the derived per-query threshold. Below this, BM25 stops discriminating.

query_token_scale.note: Scales the threshold down for short queries: 0.3 points of score per query token.

alias_token.note: An alias label as it appears in text: [[PERSON_PHONE_h2n7v5cx8m0d]]. Kept whole rather than split, because 'person' and 'phone' are boilerplate shared by every label of that field type and would make two different people's memories score alike. Mirrors synap/cloud/shared/tokenizer.py — keep the two in step.

bm25.suffix_note: Order matters: longest-first, because _stem returns on first match. Reordering this list silently changes every stem and therefore every BM25 score.

env_flags.$comment: Read at CALL time, never at module load. Python does os.environ.get inside the function bodies; JS must do the same or late process.env mutation stops working and the flag looks broken. See gotcha G-S.

SYNAP_SDK_CACHE_HONOR_TTL_HINT.note: A bundle's server ttl_hint_seconds may only SHORTEN the global TTL, never extend it.

SYNAP_SDK_CACHE_INVALIDATE_ON_WRITE.note: 2026-07-16 eval register issue #8: the cloud invalidates its own Redis caches on ingest, but that stops at the process boundary.

SYNAP_SDK_CACHE_MAX_ENTRY_AGE.note: 2026-07-16 eval register issue #6: stored_at is a sliding lease renewed on hit, so under steady traffic a pre-update snapshot never expired. Defaults to 2x the sliding TTL; 0 disables.

coverage_gate.note: Fraction of the query's stems present in the picked items. A bundle can clear the BM25 threshold on one shared token ('account') while lacking the asked-for fact entirely: the false HIT behind the eval's 'forgot the name' failure. ALWAYS computed and reported; ENFORCED only when SYNAP_SDK_CACHE_COVERAGE_MIN is explicitly set, so default behavior is unchanged. When it does fire it must gate BEFORE any side effect, so a rejected lookup leaves cache state untouched.

rejected_items_cap.note: Rejected items reported per lookup, highest score first, so a large cache cannot bloat the payload.

rung_key.$comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for how a scope rung is written on the wire and compared in both SDK anticipation caches. The server stamps a pushed bundle with this string (ContextBundleProto.anticipation_scope_rung) and each SDK builds the same string from the `scope` path its own fetch names; a bundle is servable only when the two agree. Three implementations exist by necessity (server Python, SDK Python, SDK TypeScript) because the producer is not an SDK, so the vectors below are what stops them drifting.
rung_key.note: Node ids are deliberately not what travels. They are registry surrogates and an SDK in a customer's process has never seen one; a caller names a rung with level keys and its own external ids, so that is the vocabulary the comparison happens in. Level keys are ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ so they can hold neither separator and only the value needs escaping.
rung_key.sort: by level key, ascending, plain codepoint order
rung_key.escape_order: backslash first. Reversing it makes `a|b` and `a\pb` encode to the same string, which is a false match between two different rungs.
rung_key.absent: null (an empty proto string on the wire) means the bundle or the request named no rung. Serving requires the two to be EQUAL, so absent matches only absent. That leaves every client without nested scoping byte-identical to today and refuses every genuinely cross-rung serve; the cost of the rule being wrong is a cold fetch, and the cost of a subset rule being wrong is one person's context handed to another.

vectors.note: insertion order must not change the key; a dict has whatever order the caller wrote and ladder order is not available here
the escape-order case: this must NOT collide with a|b above
sorted by key, so `customer=ab` and this cannot collapse

semantic_match.$comment: Matching a fetch query to prefetched items by meaning, with the SDK's local embedding model (`model`, which history search uses too). An item's score is its best cosine to the query, over the item's own text and the questions it answers (its HQEs, sent with the bundle item; item_questions), with the query as asked and with the asker's pronouns in the third person (canonical_query). Three bands: at sure_min_cosine or above the cache answers; between min_cosine and sure_min_cosine the match is borderline and the SDK asks the server too, serving the server's answer if it arrives within race_deadline_ms and the cached one if not; below min_cosine the server answers. A hit also serves items at serve_min_cosine or above, and items from a bundle holding a hit at bundle_serve_min_cosine or above. asked_kind: a question that asks for a time of day, a duration or an amount is not answered by served items holding none (asked_details). Items not embedded yet, and every item without the model, are matched as before (BM25 with its novel-term gate). The thresholds hold for `model` only, one text per run. Measured on harnesses/anticipation_match (404 labelled queries, 4 languages, production-shaped bundles with production-prompt HQEs), held-out half, per 100 questions with the answer cached for 68: BM25 served 27 right and 13 wrong; MiniLM on the memory text alone 30 and 5.5; with all of the above (sure bar 0.74) 44-47 and 2.5-3, 21 Oct 2026.

self_pronouns.$comment: canonical_query rewrites the asker's own pronouns into the third person memories are stored in ('my landlord' -> 'the user's landlord'). Applied in order, case-insensitive. 'canon' compares only the rewritten query, 'both' takes the better of the two (HQEs are written in the first person).

asked_details.$comment: asked_kind: a question that asks for one of these kinds of value is not answered by served items that hold none (asked 'what time is my flight', served 'the flight is on 25 October'). Its own list, not history_search.asked_kinds, so history search's ranking is untouched. Query patterns are matched case-insensitively; value patterns are written to be language-neutral (digits, units, currency) and avoid \\b next to non-ASCII letters, which ECMAScript's \\b does not treat as word characters.

time_of_day.query: what time|at what time|which time|opening hours|open hours|what hours|when does .{0,40}(open|close|start|begin)|qu[eé] hora|a qu[eé] hora|que horas|a que horas|hor[aá]rio|किस समय|कितने बजे|टाइम

duration.query: how long|duration|how many (minutes|hours)|cu[aá]nto dura|cu[aá]nto tiempo|quanto tempo|dura[cç][aã]o|कितनी देर|कितने समय

money.query: how much|cost|price|fee|charge|budget|amount|quote|cu[aá]nto cuesta|precio|costo|tarifa|quanto custa|pre[cç]o|valor|custo|कितने पैसे|कितना पैसा|कीमत|खर्च|शुल्क|कितने रुपये

history_search.$comment: Local search over the raw turns a compaction replaced (COMPACTION_HYBRID_PLAN.md P5). Keyword first (literal values, then BM25 with the bm25 section's tokenizer), embeddings only when installed and keywords come up short; results fused by reciprocal rank with a small recency prior, shown in conversation order. The heading reaches the LLM prompt: byte-identical in both SDKs. Each hit brings the turn before it (its last previous_turn_words words). Irregular past forms are mapped to the base form before stemming (English; history search only). A turn needs min_matched_terms query words, or one word found in at most rare_term_max_share of the turns. Passages (passages, passages_per_turn): a turn longer than max_words_per_excerpt is scored as passages (table rows with their header, a few lines of a log, a few sentences), ranks by its best passage, and shows its best passages; measured 20 Oct with multilingual MiniLM, answer text found 117 of 148 probes vs 93 by whole turns. Tool results the host agent reports are archived here too, never sent to the server, as "[tool result: <name>] <result>" cut to tool_result_max_chars: searchable like turns, not counted as server turns.
history_search.heading: ### From the earlier turns (verbatim excerpts matched to the latest message; later turns may have changed them)

early_query.note: A question about how things started: no recency prior for it, or later turns on the same subject push the early one out (20 Oct, documents case).

asked_kinds.$comment: A question that asks for a kind of value (a number to call, an email, an address, an amount, a date, a percentage) also ranks the passages that hold one, among those sharing a query word: 'the best number to reach Renata' found her email but showed 'Best, Renata', not the line with the number (20 Oct).
